analysis.one_liner: Grasim Industries is the Aditya Birla Group's diversified holding company — it controls UltraTech (India's largest cement maker), and directly runs viscose/cellulosic fibre and chemicals businesses plus newer bets in decorative paints (Birla Opus) and B2B e-commerce (Birla Pivot).
tags: Consol. net loss this qtr (one-off charge)
Promoter stake up to 45.2%, zero pledge
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter to Sept 2026) were announced on November 13, 2026: consolidated revenue hit a record ₹50,105 crore (+26% YoY) and EBITDA grew 25% to ₹6,513 crore, but the company reported a consolidated net loss of ₹234 crore (versus a ₹595 crore profit a year ago) because of a ₹767 crore exceptional impairment charge tied to its Canadian pulp joint venture, AV Group NB. Standalone (parent-only) PAT rose 187% YoY to ₹2,306 crore, largely because the parent booked a ₹3,968 crore dividend received from UltraTech Cement, which gets eliminated at consolidation.
analysis.plain_terms: The tension here: revenue and operating profit (EBITDA) are genuinely growing at double digits across cement, fibre and chemicals, but the headline 'profit' swung to a loss purely because of a one-off writedown in a small overseas pulp venture - not because the core businesses are struggling. Separately, the eye-catching 187% jump in the standalone PAT figure is mostly Grasim collecting a dividend cheque from its own subsidiary UltraTech, not new operating earnings, so it shouldn't be read as the underlying business tripling.
analysis.quarters: Consolidated revenue and EBITDA grew ~25-26% YoY, driven by UltraTech cement volumes (+12.9% to 38.2 MT) and cellulosic fibres (EBITDA +49% YoY to ₹522 crore). Chemicals EBITDA fell 11% YoY despite 15% revenue growth - margin pressure there. Birla Opus (paints) plus Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce) combined EBITDA loss widened to roughly ₹320 crore from ₹140 crore in Q1 FY27. Management called the pulp-JV charge one-off, cautioned that standalone numbers are distorted by the UltraTech dividend timing, and reiterated Birla Pivot is targeting EBITDA breakeven by FY27 exit, with paints profitability tied to reaching ₹10,000 crore of revenue by FY28.
analysis.performance_read: The only corporate action in the verified data is a 5:1 split in October 2016, already reflected in the price series - no demerger or bonus distortion to adjust for here. Long-term returns are strong: 1Y +9.56% versus Nifty -2.84% and peer UltraTech +3.46%; 3Y +58.36% versus Nifty +27.8%; 5Y +67.83% versus Nifty +38.85%. The recent 3M -6.61% and the pullback from the ₹3,380.5 peak (Aug 10, 2026) to ₹3,034 now (-10.2%) look like a routine correction within a multi-year uptrend, not a crash.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 35.95x trailing P/E and 2.03x P/B, the stock is not statistically cheap. Part of why it carries this multiple is structural: as a holding company, its reported earnings are currently muddied by the one-off pulp JV impairment and by intercompany dividend timing between standalone and consolidated accounts, so the trailing EPS used in that P/E may not reflect normalized earnings. ROE of ~4.97% looks weak but is partly a holding-company artifact; ROCE of ~9.29% is a more useful but still unspectacular reference for a capital-intensive group. Whether it is actually cheap or expensive can't be settled from this data alone - check a normalized (ex-exceptional) consolidated EPS on Screener before trusting the headline P/E.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is broad-based and largely volume-led: cement volumes up 12.9% YoY, cellulosic fibre EBITDA up strongly, and Birla Opus paints revenue up 35% YoY as a new entrant gaining share from a small base. But chemicals EBITDA fell even as its revenue grew, showing margin compression, and the two newer ventures (paints, B2B e-commerce) are still loss-making, so consolidated profit growth is lagging revenue growth for now.
analysis.health_read: Setting aside the one-off impairment, operating cash generation across UltraTech, fibre and chemicals looks healthy given the EBITDA growth. One source puts consolidated net debt/EBITDA at an improving 1.45x (from 1.62x) as of mid-2026, but another cites a much higher consolidated debt-to-equity of ~1.97x - these don't reconcile cleanly; Not verified, check on Screener. The more immediate concern looks like business risk - the pulp JV writedown and still-loss-making paints/e-commerce arms - rather than balance-sheet distress.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (Aditya Birla Group) increased their stake from 43.74% to 45.20% in the September 2026 quarter, and pledged promoter shareholding has stayed at 0% across all recent quarters - a clean, improving ownership picture. FII holding stood near 17.18% and DII near 16.28% as of March 2026; no single marquee or famous individual investor name surfaced in search results as holding a notable stake, so if looking for one on the register, none was found.
strengths: Record consolidated quarterly revenue of ₹50,105 crore, up 26% YoY in Q2 FY27
Cellulosic fibres EBITDA up 49% YoY to ₹522 crore on strong realisations
Promoter stake raised to 45.20% (from 43.74%) with 0% pledge across recent quarters
1Y stock return of +9.56% outperformed both Nifty (-2.84%) and peer UltraTech (+3.46%)
watchpoints: Consolidated net loss of ₹234 crore this quarter from a ₹767 crore exceptional impairment in the Canadian pulp JV, AV Group NB
Birla Opus (paints) + Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce) combined EBITDA loss widened to ~₹320 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹140 crore in Q1 FY27
Chemicals segment EBITDA fell 11% YoY despite 15% revenue growth, signalling margin pressure
Stock is down 10.2% from its August 10, 2026 peak of ₹3,380.5
analysis.one_thing: Whether Birla Opus and Birla Pivot narrow their combined EBITDA loss toward the targeted FY27-exit breakeven - watch the segment EBITDA lines for paints and B2B e-commerce in the Q3/Q4 FY27 results to see if consolidated profit growth starts catching up to the revenue growth already visible.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 figures were cross-checked against the official grasim.com press release (revenue ₹50,105 crore, EBITDA ₹6,513 crore, consolidated net loss ₹234 crore, standalone PAT ₹2,306 crore up 187%); a third-party claim of consolidated EBITDA ₹9,722 crore and a separate claim of standalone PAT growth of 316.7% were set aside as outliers that disagreed with the company's own release. Valuation metrics (P/E 35.95x, P/B 2.03x, ROE 4.97%, ROCE 9.29%) and two conflicting debt figures (D/E 1.97x versus net debt/EBITDA 1.45x) came from aggregator sites, not a single primary filing - please verify on Screener. Promoter shareholding increase (43.74% to 45.20%) and zero pledge were cross-checked across two independent aggregator sources.
